name: New Jersey
sources: Brackets: NJ-1040 Tax Rate Schedules, 2020 and after (Table A single/MFS, Table B MFJ/HoH/QW) — https://www.disabilityombudsman.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/current/njtaxratesch.pdf (index: https://www.nj.gov/www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/taxtables.shtml)

Exemptions ($1,000 regular, $1,000 age 65+, $1,500 per dependent) and medical expenses over 2% of income: 2025 Form NJ-1040 lines 6-12, 31 — https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/current/1040.pdf; NJ Division of Taxation — https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/njit13.shtml
Property tax deduction (lesser of taxes paid or $15,000; half each for spouses filing separately in the same home): https://nj.gov/treasury/taxation/njit35.shtml

No 2026 rate/exemption changes: FY2026 budget (https://www.mccarter.com/insights/new-jersey-fy-2026-budget-tax-law-changes/) and FY2027 budget (EY Tax News 2026-1456, https://taxnews.ey.com/news/2026-1456) change only QSBS, the alternative business calculation and the child tax credit
provisional: The 2026 NJ-1040 is not yet published; rate schedules, exemptions and the $15,000 property-tax cap are statutory (not indexed) and taken from the 2025 forms, with no 2026 change found
Married filing separately property-tax cap set to $7,500 on the assumption that spouses share one home (each may use half the taxes)
notes: New Jersey's refundable child tax credit, retirement income exclusion, and ANCHOR / Senior Freeze property-tax relief are not included.
New Jersey does not allow the federal deduction for half of self-employment tax, so self-employed filers may owe a little more than shown.
